scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A rocket weighing hundreds of tonnes lifts off and reaches space in minutes. What pushes it up there?

scenes.name: newton
scenes.text: Rockets follow Newton's third law. Push hot gas down hard, and the gas pushes the rocket up.

scenes.name: burn
scenes.text: Fuel burns with an oxidiser, carried on board because there's no air in space to burn with.

scenes.name: nozzle
scenes.text: The bell shaped nozzle speeds the exhaust up to several kilometres per second, making a huge thrust.

scenes.name: stages
scenes.text: Rockets drop empty stages as they climb, so they don't waste fuel carrying dead weight.

scenes.name: orbit
scenes.text: Reaching orbit is mostly about going sideways fast, nearly eight kilometres per second, so you keep falling around Earth.

scenes.name: isro
scenes.text: Many launch sites sit near the equator and face east, to borrow speed from Earth's spin.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Push gas down, drop stages, go sideways fast. Follow for more on how things really work.
